A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Momentum-SAM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR100 and ImageNet training experiments, WMT 2016 translation results, and optimizer analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds momentum-overshooting diagnostics and feature-rank measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same normalized negative-momentum perturbation and optimizer updates. The unnormalized, adaptive, and BatchNorm-only variants already appear in v1; expanded explanations do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR100 and ImageNet image classification and WMT 2016 English-to-Romanian translation. Translation moves from A.10 to A.9. The added diagnostics use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Figure A.15 adds plotted AE-SAM comparisons in the three CIFAR100 model panels, absent from the corresponding v1 Figure A.3. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables and translation comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: The existing benchmark training settings remain unchanged, but v2 A.3 introduces substantial new diagnostic protocols: constant versus decaying learning rates, comparisons before and after momentum updates, independent validation-gradient controls, and learning-rate, momentum, and batch-size scans. A.5 additionally measures feature rank before pooling.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled overshooting investigations across architectures and hyperparameters in A.3, feature-rank analysis in A.5, and two-direction loss landscapes in A.11. These substantially extend the mechanistic evidence. Existing normalization, curvature, warm-up, and equal-budget analyses are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: v2 Figure A.2 explicitly reports averaging the new loss-landscape diagnostic over 30 runs. The existing 68% Student-t confidence-interval practice and five-run baseline estimates for ImageNet uncertainty remain unchanged; increased repetitions of retained experiments are not established.

E6.justification: Main benchmark table values and translation BLEU scores remain unchanged. Substantial new results include overshooting-control and sensitivity trajectories, AE-SAM comparison curves, and feature ranks of 5019 for SGD, 4775 for SAM, and 3791 for MSAM in A.5. These are added findings, not improved accuracy under existing benchmark settings.

T1.justification: A.1 retains Proposition 1, Setting 1, Lemma 2, Theorem 3, and their proofs. Mathematical objectives and perturbation definitions are also unchanged apart from numbering and presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claim of SAM-like benefits without substantial computational overhead remain unchanged. The introduction adds an explicit contribution concerning momentum-slope behavior beyond sharpness minimization, and the conclusion makes an unqualified claim that efficient alternatives are outperformed in both speed and accuracy.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends the overshooting explanation through interpretations of momentum updates, learning-rate decay, and independent validation gradients, and argues that negative alignment is not caused by limited sampling. A.5 adds a feature-rank explanation involving more distinct, task-specific features. Section 4.1 also corrects improved generalization from a larger to a smaller train-test gap.

D1.justification: v2 A.13 newly discloses use of up to four NVIDIA A100 GPUs. It also replaces the appendix's placeholder implementation link with the repository already linked in v1's abstract, clarifying documentation without establishing new code availability. Existing preprocessing and benchmark hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Dai et al. (2023), two Andriushchenko et al. (2023) papers, and Springer et al. (2024). These extend positioning around normalization and feature-based explanations, including an explicit claimed disagreement with Dai et al.; the broader SAM-efficiency positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Existing material is substantially reorganized: normalization moves from Section 4.4 to A.2, while warm-up, implementation, optimizer-comparison details, and hyperparameter searches move behind the other appendix analyses. Sections 2.4 and 4.1 and the conclusion are reworked around momentum overshooting, and Section 4.1 is renamed.

P2.justification: v2 adds the diagnostic displays in Figures A.2–A.7 and the three-dimensional surfaces in A.13, and adds AE-SAM curves to the retained hyperparameter comparison. Former Figure 5 becomes Figure A.1. The document also changes its visual template, repositions Figure 1 and Algorithm 1, and reflows existing tables and figures.

improvement.justification: The new overshooting controls strengthen v1's existing cosine-similarity and loss-ascent evidence, while hardware disclosure and corrected generalization-gap wording improve reporting. These provide a limited net gain. The stronger blanket superiority claim exceeds Table 1's mixed evidence: LookSAM retains 83.31±0.12 versus MSAM's 83.21±0.07 on WRN-28-10.
